title: Accept an optional Idempotency-Key on the SDK resource create commands
acceptance_criteria: client.workspaces.create, client.sessions.create, client.scenes.create, client.content.createBlock and client.assets.createLink each accept an optional trailing options argument carrying an idempotencyKey and forward it as the Idempotency-Key request header, mirroring client.visibility.reveal/hide; omitting the option is unchanged and non-breaking; the header is sent through the existing transport seam (RequestSpec.idempotencyKey in packages/sdk-ts/src/http.ts) so a retried create under a reused key replays the original resource the server already dedupes (CORE-DX-004) instead of producing a duplicate; the SDK advertises an idempotency key ONLY on the create routes the server actually honors (workspace/session/scene/content-block/asset-link create), never on entity create (which has no server dedupe yet - see CORE-DX-009).
required_tests: SDK type tests assert the new options argument is OPTIONAL on each covered create method (contrast reveal/hide where idempotencyKey is required); a transport/unit test asserts a supplied idempotencyKey is emitted as the Idempotency-Key header on each covered create and that no header is sent when the option is omitted; an end-to-end/contract test shows a reused key replays the original resource through the SDK (resource count stays 1); the sdk-parity and OpenAPI drift gates stay green (no wire-contract or route change).
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (csv/Issues _from_verticals/core_gaps_Phase2.csv ARC-GAP-102). SDK-ONLY change: the server-side dedupe store, the Idempotency-Key middleware, the per-route scopes and the integration tests already exist from CORE-DX-004 (apps/api/SystemModule/IdempotentResourceCreator.cs + IdempotencyKeyHeader.cs cover workspace/session/scene/content-block/asset-link create), but the typed create methods take no options argument so a consumer cannot ask the server to dedupe without reaching past the SDK. Add the optional idempotencyKey options arg to each covered create in packages/sdk-ts/src/resources/{workspaces,sessions,scenes,content,assets}.ts and forward it via the existing RequestSpec.idempotencyKey transport (packages/sdk-ts/src/http.ts) exactly as visibility.reveal/hide do. Keep it optional and non-breaking. Update docs/08 only to note the SDK create methods accept an idempotency key. No server change in this story.

title: Honor Idempotency-Key on entity create and add the SDK passthrough
acceptance_criteria: The entity create endpoint (POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/entities) reads the optional Idempotency-Key header and routes the create through the existing IdempotentResourceCreator under a per-tenant scope (entity-create:{organizationId}), so a retried entity create under a reused key returns the original entity and creates exactly one, a different key creates a new entity, and a malformed key is rejected after authorization (400) without creating anything - matching the five create routes already covered by CORE-DX-004; client.entities.create then accepts the same optional idempotencyKey options argument and forwards the Idempotency-Key header (mirroring CORE-DX-008); entity create is added to the documented covered-routes list in docs/08.
required_tests: Integration: an entity create retried under the same Idempotency-Key returns the original entity and the entity count stays 1; a different key creates a new entity; a malformed key is 400 after auth and creates nothing (extend tests/LiveCore.Api.IntegrationTests/IdempotencyKeyEndpointTests.cs to cover entity create); an SDK type test asserts entities.create's options argument is optional and a transport test asserts the header is forwarded; the sdk-parity and OpenAPI drift gates stay green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (ARC-GAP-102). Entity create is the ONLY resource create with no server-side idempotency on either layer: apps/api/Entities/EntityEndpoints.cs CreateEntityAsync calls the EntityCreation domain service directly and never reads the header or uses IdempotentResourceCreator, and docs/08 omits entity create from the covered-routes list. Wire EntityEndpoints through the existing IdempotentResourceCreator (reuse the shared idempotency_keys store and IdempotencyKeyHeader.Read; no new infrastructure) with scope entity-create:{organizationId}, then add the entities.create SDK passthrough. Sequence the server half BEFORE the SDK passthrough so the SDK never advertises a key the server ignores. Update apps/api/Entities, packages/sdk-ts/src/resources/entities.ts, tests/LiveCore.Api.IntegrationTests/IdempotencyKeyEndpointTests.cs and the docs/08 covered-routes list. Depends on CORE-DX-008 (shares the SDK options-arg pattern).

epic: Workspace Member Roster and Role Administration
title: Add a workspace-member roster read
acceptance_criteria: A new route GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members returns the workspace's members as a paged, audience-safe projection - each entry carrying the membership id, the userProfileId, the generic MembershipRole and explicitly allow-listed audience-safe display metadata (e.g. a display name) plus server timestamps - so a host can render a members screen and obtain the membership id that client.workspaces.removeMember requires; the read is authorized to the workspace-administration roles (Owner/Admin, matching listInvitations), tenant- and workspace-scoped, and fail-closed (a non-member or a non-administration caller and a foreign or unknown workspace are hidden-404); bounded paging (items + hasMore, clamped to the platform max, per CORE-DX-003); the projection NEVER includes an invited/login email, a token, or any auth rationale (data-minimized PII discipline); the matching client.workspaces.listMembers SDK method exists.
required_tests: Integration: an Owner/Admin lists the workspace's members with each entry's membership id + generic role + audience-safe display metadata and uses a returned membership id to drive removeMember; a non-administration member and a non-member are hidden-404; a foreign-tenant workspace is hidden-404; the response carries no email/token/auth-rationale (a payload-shape assertion pins the allow-listed fields); paging clamps to the max; the sdk-parity, OpenAPI and spec-consistency drift gates stay green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (csv/Issues _from_verticals/core_gaps_Phase2.csv ARC-GAP-103). The SDK exposes the full workspace surface (list/create/get/getWithETag/update/archive/inviteMember/listInvitations/acceptInvitation/revokeInvitation/removeMember) but NO member-roster read, and the existing WorkspaceMemberResponse (packages/contracts/src/workspaces.ts) is the invitation-redemption projection returned only to the accepting user - never an administrator roster - so the membership id removeMember needs is otherwise unobtainable. Add a workspace-scoped roster read over the existing WorkspaceMember aggregate (apps/api/Workspaces; add IWorkspaceMemberRepository.ListByWorkspaceAsync(workspaceId, page)); reuse the existing tenant-resolve to workspace-membership to administration-role authorization (mirror the listInvitations route in apps/api/Workspaces/WorkspaceEndpoints.cs). Keep the projection audience-safe and product-neutral (generic identifiers + MembershipRole, no vertical vocabulary - docs/04, docs/19). No DB migration (a read over existing rows, joining audience-safe profile display metadata read-only). Add the route plus the SDK method and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json; update csv/api_routes.csv, csv/authorization_matrix.csv, docs/05, docs/06 and docs/08.

epic: Workspace Member Roster and Role Administration
title: Add a workspace-member role-change command
acceptance_criteria: A new route PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/members/{memberId} changes a member's generic MembershipRole given an UpdateWorkspaceMemberRoleRequest; it is authorized to the workspace-administration roles (Owner/Admin), tenant- and workspace-scoped, and fail-closed (a foreign or unknown member or workspace is hidden-404, a non-administration caller is denied); the last-Owner invariant is enforced - demoting the last remaining Owner is refused (409), mirroring the existing last-Owner-cannot-be-removed rule; the change honors optimistic concurrency via If-Match (a stale ETag is 412, per CORE-DX-002) and is audited (a MemberRoleChanged audit fact); the matching client.workspaces.updateMemberRole SDK method exists and returns the updated membership.
required_tests: Integration: an Owner/Admin changes another member's role and the roster reflects it; demoting the last Owner is 409; a stale If-Match is 412; a foreign-tenant or unknown member/workspace is hidden-404; a non-administration caller is denied; the change emits the MemberRoleChanged audit fact; negative-authorization cases fail closed; the sdk-parity, OpenAPI and spec-consistency drift gates stay green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (ARC-GAP-103). The workspace surface today supports only invite (POST .../members) and remove (DELETE .../members/{memberId}) - there is no role-change command anywhere (MapPatch appears nowhere in apps/api), so an administrator cannot correct a member's role without remove-and-reinvite. Add the PATCH command over the existing WorkspaceMember aggregate and authorization; reuse the audit pipeline and the unit of work; enforce the existing last-Owner invariant on demotion. Product-neutral (generic MembershipRole, no vertical terms). Add the route plus the SDK method and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json; update csv/api_routes.csv, csv/authorization_matrix.csv, csv/event_catalog.csv if an audit action is added, docs/06 and docs/08. Depends on CORE-WSM-001 (shares the roster contract and the membership id it surfaces).

title: Add a host-side workspace asset enumeration read
acceptance_criteria: A new route GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/assets returns the workspace's assets as a paged host AssetResponse projection - assetId, AssetStatus, contentType, sizeBytes, checksum and created/updated timestamps - so a host authoring surface can enumerate a workspace's uploaded assets to re-attach, reveal or delete them across page loads; the read is authorized to the host-content roles that create the upload intent (Owner/Admin/Host/CoHost), tenant- and workspace-scoped, and fail-closed (a non-member or unauthorized role and a foreign or unknown workspace are hidden-404, foreign-tenant assets never appear); bounded paging (items + hasMore, clamped to the platform max, per CORE-DX-003) with deterministic ordering; the matching client.assets.list SDK method exists. This is the HOST projection (full asset metadata for an authoring role) and is distinct from the audience-safe attachments projection on the participant visible feed (CORE-ALC-002).
required_tests: Integration: a host-content role lists a workspace's assets (all statuses) scoped to the resolved tenant and workspace; a non-member and a non-host role are hidden-404/denied; assets from another tenant or workspace never appear; paging clamps to the max with a stable order; the sdk-parity, OpenAPI and spec-consistency drift gates stay green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (csv/Issues _from_verticals/core_gaps_Phase2.csv ARC-GAP-104 part b). CORE-ALC-002 added the AUDIENCE-safe attachments projection for a REVEALED resource on the participant visible feed, but there is still no HOST-side enumeration of a workspace's assets: client.assets exposes only createUploadIntent/confirmUpload/getDownloadUrl/createLink/deleteLink/delete (packages/sdk-ts/src/resources/assets.ts) and the Assets endpoint group (apps/api/Assets/AssetEndpoints.cs) has no GET workspace-asset list - every other resource (scenes/sessions/entities/content-blocks) already has a workspace/parent-scoped list read. Add the workspace-scoped host read (IAssetRepository.ListByWorkspaceAsync, paged) plus a host AssetResponse contract and client.assets.list, reusing the existing asset authorization (same host-content roles as upload-intent). Keep it product-neutral (generic asset metadata; no handout/campaign vocabulary - those stay vertical-side). Add the route plus the SDK method and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json; update csv/api_routes.csv, csv/authorization_matrix.csv, packages/contracts/src/assets.ts, docs/06, docs/08 and docs/12.

title: Add a host per-resource attachments read
acceptance_criteria: A new host-authorized route lists the assets linked to a given target resource (a content block or entity) - GET /api/v1/assets/by-target/{targetType}/{targetId} - returning the same host AssetResponse projection (CORE-ALC-003), so a host can see and manage the attachments of one specific resource without scanning the whole workspace; the read is authorized to the host-content roles, tenant- and workspace-scoped to the target's workspace, and fail-closed (a target outside the caller's tenant/workspace is hidden-404, an unauthorized role is denied); a target with no links returns an empty page (never an error); the matching client.assets.listForResource SDK method exists. This is the HOST counterpart of the audience-safe per-resource attachments on the visible feed (CORE-ALC-002) and complements, never replaces, it.
required_tests: Integration: a host-content role lists the assets linked to a target it owns; a target in another tenant/workspace is hidden-404; an unauthorized role is denied; a target with no links returns an empty page; the sdk-parity, OpenAPI and spec-consistency drift gates stay green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (ARC-GAP-104 part b, the 'or those linked to a resource' half). OPTIONAL/complementary to CORE-ALC-003: the workspace enumeration already satisfies the primary host need; this per-resource read is an ergonomics add for an authoring surface focused on one resource. Reuse the existing AssetLink model and IAssetLinkRepository.ListByTargetAsync (apps/api/Assets/AssetLinkRepository.cs) - the same link read the audience projection uses - but gate it on the host-content roles instead of audience visibility. Product-neutral. Add the route plus the SDK method and regenerate openapi/livecore-v1.json; update csv/api_routes.csv, csv/authorization_matrix.csv, docs/08 and docs/12. Depends on CORE-ALC-003 (shares the host AssetResponse projection). The owner may defer this story if the workspace enumeration alone is sufficient.

title: Project the participant's current scene onto the visible-feed response
acceptance_criteria: ParticipantVisibleFeedResponse carries an optional currentScene field - the audience-safe ParticipantSceneResponse (id, title, order) for the scene currently active for the participant - in addition to participantId, workspaceId, items and generatedAt; currentScene is the audience-safe projection of the most-recently-revealed visible Scene in the participant's session-scoped visible set (derived from the same VisibleResourceReveal set the items are built from, using the existing RevealedAt), so a consumer can render where-we-are-now from the feed alone without enumerating workspace scenes or reaching for a host read; currentScene is null (never an error) when no scene is currently visible to the participant; it is produced ONLY through the existing role-based audience scene projection (never the raw host scene), so no host-only field leaks (threats T2/T7); the feed stays already-filtered and fail-closed.
required_tests: Integration: a participant feed shows currentScene as the latest revealed visible scene (audience-safe id/title/order only); revealing a newer scene flips currentScene; currentScene is null when no scene is visible; a host-only scene field never appears; the per-response property set is pinned to the new shape; the contract/OpenAPI/sdk-parity drift gates stay green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (csv/Issues _from_verticals/core_gaps_Phase2.csv ARC-GAP-106). CORE-APROJ-002 enriched the feed ITEM, but no story added an active/current SCENE projection to the feed RESPONSE: ParticipantVisibleFeedResponse (packages/contracts/src/visibility.ts) and its server DTO (apps/api/Visibility/ParticipantFeedDtos.cs) still carry only { participantId, workspaceId, items, generatedAt }, ParticipantSceneResponse (packages/contracts/src/scenes.ts) has no active/current marker, and SceneActivated is a host-side live signal carrying only a SceneId. Resolve currentScene through the existing Visibility-owned audience projector port (the same port CORE-APROJ-002 uses; the Visibility module may not reference Scenes directly - CORE-ARCH-001, adapter in the composition root); never recompute visibility locally. Product-neutral (Scene is already a first-class Core resource). The route shape is unchanged. Update packages/contracts/src/visibility.ts, apps/api/Visibility (the feed projection), docs/08, the OpenAPI document and the SDK type. Composes with CORE-APROJ-002. Severity low (the data is already inferable from items; this denormalizes and marks the current scene).

title: Publish the migrations runner image on release tags
acceptance_criteria: The release image-publish pipeline builds, scans, pushes and signs the migrations runner image (livecore-migrations) alongside the existing api and worker images, pinned to the release version: the publishable-image tooling accepts 'migrations' (scripts/LiveCoreImageTags.psm1 ValidateSet and scripts/derive-image-tags.ps1 emit migrations=ghcr.io/<owner>/livecore-migrations:<version>), and the CI publish job (.github/workflows/ci.yml) builds it from apps/api/Migrations.Dockerfile, runs the same Trivy SBOM/CVE gate and immutability guard, and cosign-signs + SBOM-attests + verifies it exactly as for api/worker, on every refs/tags/v* push; the publish-dry-run job builds the migrations image on a PR and never pushes; the published coordinate is version-locked to the released @livecore package version by the existing release-version assertion.
required_tests: scripts/test-image-tags.ps1 asserts a migrations=...:<version> reference derives (and the existing non-publishable component, e.g. database, still fails closed); the publish-dry-run job builds the migrations image without pushing on a PR; the release-version/publish gates stay green; scripts/boundary-scan.ps1 stays green.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (csv/Issues _from_verticals/core_gaps_Phase2.csv ARC-GAP-109). The api and worker images are ALREADY published, version-pinned, signed and SBOM-attested to ghcr.io on release tags (the CORE-OPS-009 publish job in .github/workflows/ci.yml), but the migrations runner image is built only as a throwaway local :ci tag and never pushed - scripts/LiveCoreImageTags.psm1 hard-limits the set to ValidateSet('api','worker') - so a downstream e2e harness that wants a pinned, pull-only Core must build the migrate image from Core source (crossing the no-vendor boundary). A Migrations.Dockerfile already exists (apps/api/Migrations.Dockerfile, the one-shot 'dotnet LiveCore.Api.dll migrate' runner), so this is a CI/release-tooling change only: add 'migrations' to the publishable set and mirror the api/worker build+scan+push+sign+attest steps. Product-neutral release/distribution work. Touch .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/LiveCoreImageTags.psm1, scripts/derive-image-tags.ps1 and scripts/test-image-tags.ps1. Pairs with CORE-OPS-016 (docs + Helm/Compose defaults).

title: Document the published migrations coordinate and default Helm/Compose to it
acceptance_criteria: The published migrations image coordinate (ghcr.io/<owner>/livecore-migrations:<version>, and by digest) is documented as a pull-able release artifact alongside api/worker, and the deploy defaults stop requiring an operator to build it: deploy/helm/livecore/values.yaml defaults the migrations image to the published GHCR coordinate (registry + repository + the release tag) and the Helm README drops the 'must build and push it yourself' instruction; docs/13 lists the migrations coordinate among the published, version-pinned self-hosting images and docs/23 records that the migrations image is versioned by the release tag like api/worker; an image-only Compose override that pulls the pinned Core (api + migrations) without a build: stanza is documented for downstream e2e use.
required_tests: The Helm chart renders the published migrations coordinate by default (no manual build/push step required); the storage/spec-consistency doc gates stay green; the documented image-only Compose override references the migrations coordinate and contains no build: stanza.
notes: Raised by a vertical adopter (ARC-GAP-109). Depends on CORE-OPS-015 (the image must be published before the docs and defaults can point at it). Today deploy/helm/livecore/README.md and values.yaml tell operators the migrations runner image 'must be built and pushed to a registry your cluster can reach' (the only runtime image not defaulted to GHCR), and the Compose stack (deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml) builds migrate/api from source - so there is no documented pull-only path for a pinned Core. Document the coordinate and flip the defaults. Pure docs/deploy-config change, product-neutral. Touch docs/13, docs/23, deploy/helm/livecore/values.yaml, deploy/helm/livecore/README.md and (optionally) a deploy/compose image-only override note.
